title: Pleasure you want to keep going
meaning: Bright shared pleasure can sweep you along, but wanting to continue at any cost may turn rest into a race.
text: Enjoyment together can be open and generous here. The Sun in the physical position of Svadhisthana suggests having fun visibly, sharing discoveries and creating small celebrations. The Devil in energy describes a vulnerable pull: continuing pleasure a little longer even when free choice has narrowed to “Once more”. The Chariot in emotions responds with excitement and a sense of momentum. Rest can quickly gather speed as you try to hold onto a successful evening, while stopping feels like missing its most interesting moment.

Suppose you discover one attraction after another at a local fair. Another stall, another treat, and your chosen walk becomes a route without an ending. **Shared enjoyment loses freedom when it cannot come to a close.** You may both like what is happening while finding your own pace increasingly hard to hear. A quiet ending can seem too modest beside the promise of another vivid experience, although it might be exactly what was missing.

The difficulty grows from wanting to preserve pleasure. To keep the mood going, you continue beyond the point of feeling satisfied. Afterwards, the memory holds more rushing around than enjoyment of each other's company. A pleasant stopping point gives the experience a conclusion and leaves a wish to meet it again, without an obligation to repeat it immediately.
